plan.chapterName: OpenStax Algebra and Trigonometry 2e, chapter 1: Prerequisites
plan.contextChunk: This figure is a plain black line drawing of a right circular cylinder viewed in perspective from slightly above. The top face is rendered as a complete ellipse; the bottom is a partial ellipse whose far arc is omitted, and the two are joined by straight vertical lines at the left and right silhouette edges, so the solid reads as opaque. A horizontal arrow begins at the center of the top ellipse and points to the right until it touches the rim, with the italic label r sitting just above its shaft. Outside the body of the cylinder, to the right, a vertical double-headed arrow reaches from the level of the top rim down to the level of the bottom rim and is labeled h. There is no shading, no coordinate frame, and no numerical scale anywhere in the drawing. The two arrows isolate the only two measurements the solid requires, one running across the circular cross-section and one running along the axis. The picture accompanies the surface-area formula S = 2 pi r (r + h), fixing which distance the symbol r stands for and which the symbol h stands for.

elements: opaque right circular cylinder body drawn as a black outline with no shading
top circular cap shown as a full horizontal ellipse
bottom circular cap shown as only the visible front half ellipse, with the hidden rear arc omitted
left vertical silhouette edge connecting top ellipse to bottom front ellipse
right vertical silhouette edge connecting top ellipse to bottom front ellipse
horizontal radius arrow on the top face, starting at the center of the top ellipse and pointing to the right rim
italic label r above the top radius arrow
vertical double-headed height arrow outside the cylinder on the right, aligned with the top and bottom rim levels
italic label h beside the height arrow
surface-area net view consisting of two separate circles representing the top and bottom caps
surface-area net view consisting of one rectangle representing the lateral surface unwrapped
rectangle dimension label h on the vertical side of the net rectangle
rectangle dimension label 2πr along the horizontal side of the net rectangle
radius arrow and italic r label inside one net circle
formula annotation S = 2πr² + 2πrh = 2πr(r + h), with cap and side terms visually associated with the circles and rectangle

interactions.label: radius r
interactions.teaches: Changing r widens the circular caps and also lengthens the unwrapped side rectangle, so r contributes to both the two cap areas and the circumference term in the lateral area

interactions.label: height h
interactions.teaches: Changing h stretches only the cylinder’s vertical side, leaving the circular caps the same size and affecting only the lateral surface area term

interactions.label: View
interactions.teaches: Switching to the net separates the surface into two circles and one rectangle, making the formula S = 2πr² + 2πrh visible as caps plus side

demo_steps.title: Identify the two measurements
demo_steps.narration: In the solid-cylinder view, r is the distance from the center of the top circular face to its rim, while h is the vertical distance between the two rims.

demo_steps.title: Increase the radius
demo_steps.narration: As r grows, the top and bottom caps widen, and the cylinder’s circumference also grows. This shows why r appears in both the cap term and the side term.

demo_steps.title: Increase the height
demo_steps.narration: As h grows, the cylinder stretches upward but the circular caps do not change. Only the side surface gains area.

demo_steps.title: Unwrap the surface
demo_steps.narration: The same measurements form the net: two circles of radius r plus one rectangle of height h and width 2πr. Adding those areas gives S = 2πr² + 2πrh = 2πr(r + h).

interactionPlan.geometry_notes: Use a clean black-and-white textbook style. Stroke color black #000000, background white #ffffff, no fill or very light transparent white fill for faces. Solid cylinder default dimensions: radius r = 1.25 world units, height h = 2.4 world units. Cylinder axis is vertical on screen (+Y). The top face center is at approximately (0, +1.2, 0), bottom face center at (0, -1.2, 0). In the source, the top ellipse is wide and shallow: draw the projected top cap with apparent screen width about 2.5 units and apparent ellipse height about 0.65 units. The bottom visible front arc should match the top ellipse width and curvature, positioned directly below it; omit the far/rear half so the cylinder reads opaque. Left and right silhouette edges are vertical straight black lines tangent to the ellipses. The radius arrow lies on the top cap, horizontally from the apparent ellipse center to the rightmost rim; it should be a single-headed arrow pointing right, with italic r placed just above the shaft near its right half. The height arrow is outside the cylinder to the right, separated by about 0.35 units from the cylinder rim; it is vertical, double-headed, and spans from the top rim level to the bottom rim level, with italic h centered just to its right. For the net view, lay out the rectangle in the center-right and the two circles to its left, not overlapping: rectangle width = 2πr scaled by about 0.32 for readability, rectangle height = h; each circle radius = r scaled by about 0.55 so the two circles fit beside the rectangle. Keep equal source values equal: both net circles must always have identical radius, matching the solid cylinder radius. The rectangle’s vertical dimension must equal the selected h, and its horizontal dimension must vary linearly with 2πr. Formula values: total surface area S = 2πr² + 2πrh = 2πr(r + h), cap area contribution = 2πr², lateral contribution = 2πrh.
interactionPlan.notes: Render the cylinder as vector-like curves rather than a shaded mesh: use EllipseCurve or projected circular curves with LineBasicMaterial, plus vertical line segments. If a true 3D mesh is included for picking or transition, keep material fully transparent or nearly invisible so the final appearance remains a plain line drawing. On radius changes, update ellipse width, cap curves, silhouette edge x-positions, radius arrow endpoint, net circle radii, net rectangle width, and formula term highlighting. On height changes, update vertical edge length, bottom ellipse position, height arrow endpoints, and net rectangle height. For the solid-to-net toggle, use a simple morph/fade: cylinder outlines fade out while two circles and the rectangle fade in; preserve black outlines and italic math labels.

authoredContext:
A right circular cylinder with radius r and height h has the surface area S (in square units) given by the formula S=2πr(r+h). See the figure. Find the surface area of a cylinder with radius 6 in. and height 9 in. Leave the answer in terms of π.

Right circular cylinder

A right circular cylinder with an arrow extending from the center of the top circle outward to the edge, labeled: r. Another arrow beside the image going from top to bottom, labeled: h.
